subject: maths
question: Two tangents are drawn from an external point P to a circle, touching at points A and B. If the distance from P to the center O is 13 cm, and radius is 5 cm, what is the length of tangent PA?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **tangent PA** is **perpendicular** to the **radius OA** at the point of contact **A**.

This forms a **right-angled triangle OAP** where **OP** is the **hypotenuse**.

Apply the standard **Pythagorean triplet**: (5, 12, 13).

Since **radius (OA) = 5 cm** and **hypotenuse (OP) = 13 cm**, the **tangent (PA)** must be **12 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius** of the circle (OA) = 5 cm

Distance of **external point P** from the **center O** (OP) = 13 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a **right-angled triangle**, by **Pythagoras Theorem**: **Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/217087a7add3779c10305b785935350e2de9487b6d653045b9b40d39092866e9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔOAP, ∠OAP = 90° (Radius ⊥ Tangent)

⇒ OP² = OA² + PA²

⇒ 13² = 5² + PA²

⇒ 169 = 25 + PA²

⇒ PA² = 169 − 25

⇒ PA² = 144

⇒ PA = √144

⇒ PA = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Tangent-Radius Property

The **tangent** at any point of a circle is **perpendicular** to the **radius** through the point of contact.

Tangents from an External Point

The lengths of the two **tangents** drawn from an **external point** to a circle are always **equal** (PA = PB).

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) help solve **right-triangle** geometry problems quickly.</p
